mcqs.q: Cementum is a mineralized tissue produced by:
mcqs.explain: Cementum is a collagen-based mineralized tissue produced by cementoblasts, covering the root dentin.

mcqs.q: Acellular cementum is located on the:
opts: Coronal one-half to two-thirds of the root
mcqs.explain: Acellular cementum covers the coronal one-half to two-thirds of the root; cellular cementum covers the apical part and furcations.

opts: On the apical one-third to one-half of the root and in furcation areas
mcqs.explain: Cellular cementum is located on the apical one-third to one-half of the root and in the furcation areas of multirooted teeth.

mcqs.q: Cellular cementum is distinguished from acellular cementum by the presence of:
mcqs.explain: Cellular cementum contains cementocytes located in lacunae; acellular cementum has none.

mcqs.q: Compared with acellular cementum, cellular cementum is:
mcqs.explain: Cellular cementum is considerably thicker than acellular cementum.

mcqs.q: Cementum is best examined on a:
mcqs.explain: A longitudinal ground section (e.g. of a mandibular molar) shows cementum covering the root and the acellular/cellular distribution.

mcqs.q: The incremental lines seen within cementum:
opts: Are 'rest lines' that are more mineralized than adjacent cementum
mcqs.explain: Incremental (resting) lines represent rest periods in cementum formation and are more mineralized than the adjacent cementum.

mcqs.q: Adjacent to the cementum on the root, the dentin shows the:
mcqs.explain: Tomes' granular layer of dentin lies just internal to the cementum in the root — a useful landmark when reading the slide.

mcqs.q: At the CEJ, the MOST common configuration is:
mcqs.explain: In ~60% of teeth cementum overlaps the enamel; ~30% meet edge-to-edge (butt joint); ~10% leave a gap.

mcqs.q: A 'butt joint' type of CEJ means:
opts: Cementum meets enamel edge-to-edge in a sharp line (~30%)
mcqs.explain: A butt joint is an edge-to-edge meeting of cementum and enamel in a sharp line, seen in ~30% of teeth.

mcqs.q: When enamel and cementum do NOT meet at the CEJ (~10%), the result is:
mcqs.explain: In ~10% of teeth a gap exists where enamel and cementum do not meet, leaving the sensitive root dentin exposed.

mcqs.q: On the slide, the cellular cementum's lacunae house:
mcqs.explain: Lacunae in cellular cementum contain cementocytes; their canaliculi are directed toward the periodontal (nutrient) surface.

mcqs.q: Acellular cementum is generally found where the tooth needs:
opts: Anchorage (it is the primary attachment cementum)
mcqs.explain: Acellular (primary) cementum at the cervical/coronal root provides anchorage; cellular (secondary) cementum apically allows adaptation/repair.

mcqs.q: Cementum on a ground section appears ___ relative to the root dentin:
opts: As a distinct outer layer covering the dentin surface
As scattered islands in the crown
mcqs.explain: On a ground section, cementum is identified as the outer layer covering the root dentin surface.

mcqs.q: The cell that becomes a cementocyte is a:
opts: Cementoblast that became entrapped in the matrix it secreted
mcqs.explain: Cementocytes are cementoblasts that became entrapped in the cementum matrix and now reside in lacunae.

mcqs.q: Which combination correctly matches cementum type to location?
opts: Acellular = coronal root; cellular = apical root/furcation
mcqs.explain: Acellular cementum is coronal (cervical) on the root; cellular cementum is apical and in furcations.

saqs.q: Where are acellular and cellular cementum located on the root?
saqs.a: Acellular: coronal one-half to two-thirds. Cellular: apical one-third to one-half and in furcation areas (and is thicker).

saqs.q: How do you distinguish cellular from acellular cementum on a slide?
saqs.a: Cellular cementum contains cementocytes in lacunae and is thicker; acellular cementum has no cells and is thin.

saqs.q: What are the incremental lines of cementum?
saqs.a: Resting lines representing rest periods in formation; they are more mineralized than the adjacent cementum.

saqs.q: Which dentin landmark lies adjacent to root cementum?
saqs.a: Tomes' granular layer of dentin, just internal to the cementum in the root.

saqs.q: List the three configurations of the CEJ and their frequencies.
saqs.a: Cementum overlaps enamel (~60%), butt/edge-to-edge joint (~30%), and a gap with exposed dentin (~10%).

saqs.q: Define cementum and its forming cell.
saqs.a: A collagen-based mineralized tissue covering the root, produced by cementoblasts; entrapped cementoblasts become cementocytes.
